races.name: British Stallion Studs Ebf Fillies' Restricted Novice Stakes (for Horses In Bands B, C And D) (Ebf Restricted Race Qualifier) (GBB/GBBPlus Race)
Virgin Bet Every Saturday Money Back Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Completely Random
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with a win and two places from ten starts at Goodwood specifically; the sim-going record is modest (1W2P from 10) but course familiarity and Daniel Muscutt's quiet hands are assets when held up to exploit late gaps — hood noted; 28 days since last run is fine.
runners_data.comment: Completely Random shaped well when second three starts back and arrives here in good heart after 28 days off, with experience over today's trip and going working in his favour; our rating of 110 marks him out as the one to beat from stall 4 off 138 lb.

runners_data.name: Fondo Blanco
runners_data.note: Prominent runner whose best recent form came on soft ground at 8f; the step back to 7f on good-to-firm at Goodwood (0W2P here) looks a genuine question mark, and the prominent position may be hard to secure given the congested early field.
runners_data.comment: Fondo Blanco brings distance and going experience to the table and steps in off a 21-day break looking fresh, his 103 rating marking him second-best in the field, though his two most recent runs were unplaced and he must bounce back sharply under a hefty 135 lb.

runners_data.name: Pellitory
runners_data.note: Has won twice and placed three times from twelve starts on similar going, and last-time-out winner over this exact course and distance reads very well; David O'Meara's yard is firing (3/39 over 14 days) and Tudhope will try to hold a prominent rail position throughout.
runners_data.comment: Pellitory won last time out and has experience of today's trip and conditions, but three unplaced efforts in his last five starts temper expectations; 132 lb from stall 10 is no easy task, and he'll need to reproduce that recent best.

runners_data.name: Addison Grey
runners_data.note: Won over this course and distance last time out and boasts the strongest Goodwood record in the race (3W7P from 12 on similar going); Clifford Lee will push forward from a prominent draw and Clive Cox's 5/24 trainer strike over 14 days adds confidence.
runners_data.comment: Addison Grey arrives on the back of a win last time out and has run over today's trip and going before, giving him solid claims at a competitive 131 lb; the main risk is that ninth two starts back hints at vulnerability on an off day.

runners_data.name: Forty Years On
runners_data.note: Excellent recent winning form (four wins in five before today) but much of that came on soft ground and the good-to-firm surface here is only 2W2P from six starts; 79 days off the track is the notable unknown, though George Scott's horses often return ready.
runners_data.comment: Forty Years On arrives on the back of four wins in her last five starts, with a runner-up finish two starts back the only blip in a rich vein of form, and has run over today's trip before; the concern is 79 days off the track and a hefty 130 lb to carry.

runners_data.name: The Fingal Raven
runners_data.note: Consistent Goodwood performer (14/15 runs on similar going) but the win-rate is thin (1W7P) and his tendency to run mid-pack in form figures despite a prominent style tag suggests he finishes second flight without ever accelerating sharply — tongue tie noted.
runners_data.comment: Third last time out suggests The Fingal Raven is finding his form again after a difficult mid-season, and he has experience of today's distance and going; however, he carries 127 lb from stall 14, and has been winless in his last five starts.

runners_data.name: Galeron
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with 84 days since last run and a limited record on good-to-firm (0W1P from 8 runs); Charles Hills's yard is quiet (1/17 over 14 days) and the trip drops from 8f which is not obviously ideal — requires everything to go right to feature.
runners_data.comment: Galeron shaped with promise when second three starts back and has experience over today's trip and going, with our rating of 102 putting him firmly in the mix as a leading danger; the main concern is that he returns after 84 days off and has been winless in his last five starts.

runners_data.name: Ghost Mode
runners_data.note: The sole front-runner and the key race-shaper; Rob Hornby's recent winning ride here over 7f is directly relevant and an uncontested lead on good-to-firm is his optimum scenario — the danger is a fast-finishing prominent horse getting first run off his back if he over-relaxes.
runners_data.comment: Fresh from a win last time out and with experience of today's distance and going, Ghost Mode arrives in fair heart carrying 126 lb from stall six; however, his record in recent starts shows three finishes outside the placings, suggesting consistency remains a question mark.

runners_data.name: Aalto
runners_data.note: Has two wins and four places from eleven Goodwood starts on comparable going — the course record is the standout credential; comes here after a 35-day break, carries tongue tie, and Cieren Fallon will aim to sit just behind the prominent group and pounce late off the bend.
runners_data.comment: Ranked well down the field on our figures and up against it in a deep-looking contest, Aalto does arrive third last time out and with a win two starts back to his name, and he has experience of today's trip and conditions, but his rating of 92 makes him hard to fancy at face value.

runners_data.name: Carnival Of Light
runners_data.note: Won twice on soft at Stanneylands then flopped on soft at Goodwood last time; the sim-going record on good-to-firm (0W0P from 2) is a red flag and only 9 days between runs is a short turnaround — harder to place in a prominent position than the style tag implies.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures and with a speed rating that makes her hard to fancy at the weights, Carnival Of Light does bring a recent unbeaten run of two wins into this contest and has run over today's trip, though her latest start ended in an unplaced effort.

runners_data.name: Darkness
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old hold-up type with visor; his form on this course (2W2P from 12 on similar going) is not without merit but recent figures of 760006 show a horse who has gone completely cold, and Mark Winn on an out-of-form veteran makes this an unlikely winner.
runners_data.comment: Darkness has been winless in his last six starts, finishing no better than sixth in that sequence, and ranked 12 of 15 on our figures he looks up against it here; he has run over today's trip and going before, and 29 days since his last outing suggests he arrives fresh.

runners_data.name: Rhoscolyn
runners_data.note: True hold-up horse whose natural closing style is compressed by the field's make-up — eight years old with a blank recent record (500500) and only 7 days between runs; even on his best day his sim-going and course record (0W0P) offer little encouragement, and the redistribution out of his preferred rearward position compounds the difficulty.
runners_data.comment: Rhoscolyn has run over today's trip and going, which counts in his favour, but he heads here winless in his last six starts with unplaced efforts dominating his recent form; back quickly after just seven days, he carries 118 lb from stall nine.

runners_data.name: Leadman
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up type who, with the field's density of closers, will struggle to find the clear run his style demands; does have a Goodwood win on similar going in his last five and Kieran O'Neill is capable, but the redistributed mapping and a modest 14-day trainer stat (1/15) dampen expectations.
runners_data.comment: Leadman has won in his last six starts but that sole success is sandwiched between a string of moderate efforts, and ranking thirteenth of fifteen on our figures makes him hard to fancy; he does have experience over today's trip and going, and 21 days between runs suggests he arrives fresh.

runners_data.name: Rare Change
runners_data.note: A natural off-the-pace runner whose recent placed efforts came on soft or at Stanneylands rather than good-to-firm Goodwood; hood noted, and three wins from eight on similar going is better than it looks — but like the other redistributed hold-up types, the compact field shape works against her getting a clear passage in the straight.
runners_data.comment: Rare Change has finished seventh in each of his last two starts and ranks 14th of 15 on our figures, making him hard to fancy; he does at least return fit on 13 days' rest and has experience of today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Ironwill
runners_data.note: Natural prominent runner who cannot get that position in this crowded early field and is consequently mapped to midfield — the redistribution (STYLE_FIT 0.92) is the headline risk; his two wins at 7f on this course type are genuine credentials for a clear-run scenario, but J F Egan may find the race has gone in front of him before he can respond.
runners_data.comment: Ironwill showed his best when winning three starts back and was second two starts back, but has disappointed since, finishing unplaced last time out just eight days ago; he has run over today's trip and going, carries 116 lb from stall 11, and our rating of 95 suggests more is possible.

races.paceDynamic: Ghost Mode is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with only one horse looking to lead from the gate, Rob Hornby should be able to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front without being pressured into suicidal fractions. However, the prominent band is severely congested — Fondo Blanco, Pellitory, Addison Grey, Forty Years On, The Fingal Raven and Carnival Of Light all want to race in the first three or four positions, creating a near-certain scrimmage for ground between two and three furlongs out as that group tries to find daylight simultaneously. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than can realistically secure their natural position; Ghost Mode will take the lead, and the most likely early settlers just off the pace are Addison Grey and Pellitory given their recent Goodwood course form, while Forty Years On and Fondo Blanco may find themselves crowded back further than ideal. The resulting shape — a controlled pace set by one horse with a wall of prominent types poised just behind — unambiguously favours horses who can travel smoothly in the first two or three positions without wasting energy in traffic, meaning prominent-to-midfield runners with a good turn of foot on good-to-firm turf hold the clearest tactical advantage.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Ghost Mode Dictates, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Ghost Mode sets a moderate, uncontested pace and the prominent trio just off him get a clean run into the straight.
scenarios.body: Ghost Mode dictates at a tempo that keeps hold-up horses out of the race, and a horse tracking him in second or third has the first run to the line with momentum already built. The good-to-firm turf rewards those who travel sweetly in the first half of the race and can quickly shift gears in the Goodwood straight.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Scrimmage Opens Gap
scenarios.trigger: If the congested prominent group checks each other two furlongs out and a horse just off the pace exploits the gap.
scenarios.body: The inevitable jostling between Fondo Blanco, The Fingal Raven, Carnival Of Light and others creates a pocket of space that a sharp-actioned midfield runner can dart through. Aalto and Completely Random, travelling from just off the main pack, are best placed to capitalise on a chaotic straight.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Quickens, Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Forty Years On or Carnival Of Light aggressively challenges Ghost Mode early, turning the race into a true test of stamina.
scenarios.body: A genuine pace battle would empty the front runners and open the door for horses coming from further back in the closing stages, but the redistributed hold-up types in this field are not true closers and that limits the pool of genuine beneficiaries. Aalto, who has strong Goodwood form over this exact trip, and Completely Random are the most credible threats from off the pace.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Low Draw, Lone Leader Pinged Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Ghost Mode steals a decisive break from the gate and none of the prominent group can close the gap in the short Goodwood straight.
scenarios.body: If Hornby judges pace perfectly and the prominent field burns itself out competing for second, Ghost Mode could simply not be caught, as has happened before on this track when a single front-runner controls every fraction. This scenario requires things to go perfectly for the Balding runner but his recent winning course form and good-to-firm record keep it alive.

watchPoints.text: Ghost Mode (Rob Hornby) — watch how quickly he is allowed to stride on from the start; if Hornby is permitted to set fractions unchallenged through the first two furlongs the race could be effectively over before the turn.

Prominent congestion between Fondo Blanco, Forty Years On, The Fingal Raven and Carnival Of Light — all four will vie for the same two or three positions between two and three furlongs out, and any shuffling or checking there will directly decide whether Addison Grey or Pellitory gets first run.

Forty Years On — 79 days off the track is the single biggest unknown in the race; if George Scott has him spot-on he is the highest-class horse on recent form figures, but a rusty return on quick ground could see him drop out of contention abruptly.

Ironwill — watch his position at the two-furlong pole; if J F Egan is still tracking the congested midfield group without daylight at that point, his chance of getting to the prominent position his style demands is essentially gone.

Aalto (Cieren Fallon) — strong Goodwood course stats make him the most interesting hold-up type in the race; watch whether Fallon gets a clean run around the home turn, as any trouble-in-running in a 15-runner field on the short straight here can quickly end a hold-up horse's chance.

races.name: Virgin Bet A Good Bet Handicap Stakes (gbbplus Race)

runners_data.name: Lord Melbourne
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with solid Goodwood course form (two wins/places in similar going) but arriving on an 84-day absence for Ralph Beckett; will be in the thick of the positional battle and how Hector Crouch navigates the early congestion is decisive.
runners_data.comment: Lord Melbourne has run over today's trip and going before and, carrying 142 lb off a mark of 96, arrives here 84 days since his last start with our rating putting him right in contention — though his recent string of out-of-the-money finishes means he remains yet to score in his last five starts.

runners_data.name: High Degree
runners_data.note: William Haggas's 4-year-old is the lone front-runner with outstanding Goodwood Good-ground credentials (9/11 placed); 13 days since last run is a minor negative but Cieren Fallon's course familiarity and the horse's headgear (has raced in headgear previously) ensure he is optimally set up to dictate.
runners_data.comment: High Degree arrives on the back of a win last time out and has prior experience of today's going, so conditions should hold no fears; the main risk is whether he can reproduce that form under a stiff 141 lb.

runners_data.name: Too Soon
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse stepping up significantly to 1m4f on Good To Firm from a soft-ground win last time; Warren Fentiman claiming 3lb is useful weight relief, but 84 days off and a going question mark mean this is a scenario-dependent runner rather than a pace-shape natural.
runners_data.comment: Too Soon brings strong recent form — a winner last time out and carrying just 140 lb with an official mark of 94 — and has experience of today's distance and going. The 84-day absence is the one factor to weigh up.

runners_data.name: Tony Montana
runners_data.note: Kevin Philippart De Foy's 6-year-old wants a prominent position but 13 out of 15 Good-ground runs already on his record and a modest recent string (20-684) suggest he is operating close to his ceiling; Clifford Lee will need to avoid the scrimmage or risk burning out early.
runners_data.comment: Tony Montana shaped with promise when second five starts back, and he has experience over today's trip and going, but he has been winless in recent starts and must bounce back from a modest run 32 days ago, with his rating of 105 marking him as the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Rathgar
runners_data.note: Jack Channon's 6-year-old is actually the most interesting prominent runner — three wins and six places from 11 Good-going runs, finished 1-1-3 in his last three Goodwood outings, and David Probert knows this track; gets his head in front when he secures a clean prominent position.
runners_data.comment: Rathgar won twice in his last six starts but has since slipped to unplaced last time out, and a ninth three starts back tempers expectations; he has run over today's trip and going, carries 139 lb, and our rating of 97 sits a touch above his official 93, ranking him fifth of nine.

runners_data.name: Haku
runners_data.note: Charles Bishop partners a genuine hold-up type whose one Goodwood Good-going placing (3rd at 12f) is the only slim evidence on turf quick enough for today; at OR 88 with modest recent form (513-73) he needs the pace to collapse for this to work.
runners_data.comment: Haku showed up with a third last time out and a winner four starts back, so he retains ability, but that seventh two starts back is a concern; he has run over today's trip and going, carries 134 lb off an official mark of 88, and a 28-day break leaves fitness to prove.

runners_data.name: Oneforthegutter
runners_data.note: Ian Williams's 7-year-old is a hold-up specialist with headgear (tongue-tie/pads) and a dismal recent form string (8-7887) largely compiled over longer distances on soft or slow ground; no realistic evidence of competing on Good To Firm Goodwood, and Kieran O'Neill faces a tough task.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, with three eighths and two sevenths the sum of his recent efforts, Oneforthegutter is hard to fancy from eighth in the ratings here, though he has run over today's trip and going before and returns on a reasonable 21-day break.

runners_data.name: Classical Allusion
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's 4-year-old wants a prominent pitch but limited Good-going evidence at Goodwood (2 from 5 in similar conditions) and a tendency to underperform at the track (14th last visit); Rob Hornby will need him to avoid the positional scrum entirely.

runners_data.name: Green Sky
runners_data.note: Rod Millman's 6-year-old has sharp recent form (three wins from last four at 12-14f on Good ground) and Charlie Tucker claims 7lb, but its natural style is hold-up racing — mapped into midfield because the rear is congested — meaning it will likely race out of role and the STYLE_FIT discount is material in a pace shape dominated by a single front-runner.
runners_data.comment: Green Sky has shown she can win, with victories two, three and four starts back, but she is ranked last of all runners on our figures and that speed rating of 74 is hard to dismiss, even with the fourth last time out suggesting no obvious decline; distance and going experience at least means conditions hold no fresh unknowns.

races.paceDynamic: High Degree is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with a clear roll from the gate on Good To Firm ground at Goodwood, Cieren Fallon can dictate a measured, uncontested gallop over this 1m4f trip — a course where he already holds a strong record with nine places from eleven Good-going runs. Behind him, Lord Melbourne, Tony Montana, Rathgar, and Classical Allusion all want prominent berths, meaning four horses will be scrapping for two or three positions approaching the home turn, creating traffic turbulence at the two-to-three-furlong marker. Green Sky is a genuine hold-up horse shuffled into the midfield map because the rear is already crowded; its true tactical role is racing from off the pace, but its chance is tempered by a field shape that does not naturally free up room for late closers. This race shape strongly favours hold-up horses with proven finishing kicks on Good To Firm turf who can exploit the prominent logjam — but above all it is the prominent runners with the pace judgement to sit just off High Degree without getting embroiled in the scrimmage who are best placed; High Degree itself, if allowed to control fractions, is the primary threat. The field holds more prominent-biased types than can all secure their natural position; of the four scramblers, Rathgar and Lord Melbourne have the clearest recent Goodwood form to actually win the battle for the favoured spots, while Tony Montana and Classical Allusion risk being crowded out.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: High Degree Controls Wire
scenarios.trigger: If High Degree is allowed to bowl along at a comfortable gallop and no rival has the pace or intent to press him through the first mile.
scenarios.body: Fallon sets an honest but unhurried tempo on the front end, denying rivals a target, and the energy expenditure in the prominent scrimmage leaves challengers one-paced in the straight; High Degree, with elite Goodwood form (nine Good-going placings, two wins) and a 13-day freshness advantage, simply quickens clear at the two-furlong pole.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Scrimmage Backfires
scenarios.trigger: If the congestion among Lord Melbourne, Tony Montana, Rathgar, and Classical Allusion turns scrappy early and burns those horses out before the straight.
scenarios.body: One or two prominent runners use excessive energy jostling for position on the sweeping Goodwood bend, leaving them flat in the final two furlongs; a hold-up horse sitting patiently in genuine rear-midfield finds a clear run as the prominent pack wilts and picks them off.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Late
scenarios.trigger: If High Degree's fractions are fractionally too quick for the conditions and the prominent pack is unable to sustain the tempo into the straight.
scenarios.body: The field compresses in the final quarter-mile as High Degree ties up, promoting the most stamina-laden prominent survivor into contention; a horse who has settled just behind the scrimmage and avoided the energy drain emerges as the beneficiary.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Late Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the early gallop is genuinely strong enough to gut the field and genuine hold-up horses find daylight in the straight.
scenarios.body: This scenario is materially discounted because the true hold-up runners (Green Sky, Haku, Oneforthegutter, Too Soon) face a pace shape that does not reliably create a strong enough tempo to suit them — Green Sky is not even in its natural role — and Goodwood's run-in does not reward wide, late efforts when the pace is controlled.

watchPoints.text: High Degree (Cieren Fallon) — if he breaks cleanly and is allowed to stride into an uncontested lead, the field must chase him through the home turn; watch whether any prominent runner has the audacity to go with him in the first two furlongs.

Positional scrimmage between Rathgar, Lord Melbourne, Tony Montana, and Classical Allusion on the approach to Goodwood's sweeping bend — traffic flashpoint two to three furlongs out could produce interference and cause one of these runners to lose all momentum.

Green Sky (Charlie Tucker 7lb) — watch its early position in the first furlong; if Tucker attempts to push forward to escape the hold-up pack it will race entirely out of role, inflating its early energy cost and undermining the case built on recent wins.

Too Soon — returning from 84 days off on noticeably faster ground than its recent form (Good To Firm vs Soft wins); Warren Fentiman should be monitored for any signs the horse is not handling the quicker surface in the first half of the race.

Haku and Oneforthegutter — both genuine hold-up types near the back; if the tempo is genuinely strong in the middle portion of the race (watch splits after the half-mile), these two could be the beneficiaries in Scenario B, but their recent form gives limited reason for optimism.

races.name: Virgin Bet Celebration Mile Stakes (Group 2)

runners_data.name: Boiling Point
runners_data.note: Sole confirmed front-runner who can dictate an uncontested pace; excellent course record and sim-going strike rate of 12/15 on fast ground is the standout angle, though his recent form over 9-10f suggests the step back to 1m may help rather than hinder.
runners_data.comment: Boiling Point arrives on the back of a placed effort last time out and has experience of today's trip and conditions, with 133 lb from stall one his key test.

runners_data.name: Ebt's Guard
runners_data.note: Daniel Tudhope rides a five-year-old with strong course familiarity — five of his last five runs are over this exact trip at Goodwood — and his one win in that sequence came here; prominent style suits an uncontested pace scenario where first run counts.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Ebt's Guard nonetheless showed a hint of form with a third three starts back, and 21 days between runs leaves him reasonably fresh; however, ranked sixth of nine on our assessment, he looks a midfield proposition at best.

runners_data.name: Fast Tracker
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's gelding is a genuine hold-up horse by inclination, placed in midfield here only because the rear is oversubscribed; a 177-day absence is a significant fitness query, and racing out of his natural back-of-field role reduces his chance if the pace fails to truly develop.
runners_data.comment: Unexposed and open to improvement, Fast Tracker returns after 177 days off carrying 133 lb from stall 5, with a win two starts back hinting at ability worth respecting on his reappearance.

runners_data.name: Naqeeb
runners_data.note: Ryan Sexton takes the ride on a hold-up horse with the strongest sim-going record in the field (14/15) and a win over 10f on soft; held up among a cluster of closers, he needs a genuine pace to find clear daylight, and at OR=110 his ceiling may be tested at Group 2 level.
runners_data.comment: Naqeeb landed a win four starts back but has managed only fifth, fifth on either side of a runner-up finish in his last three outings, and 49 days off the track adds a fitness query; he has run over today's trip and going before, though 133 lb is a stiff ask.

runners_data.name: Qirat
runners_data.note: Hector Crouch partners a five-year-old who carries headgear (tongue tie) and has won twice at Goodwood, including at 7f, so a sharp finish would suit; hold-up style leaves him reliant on pace materialising, but his best performances have come fresh and on fast surfaces.
runners_data.comment: Qirat brings a win three starts back and has run over today's trip and going, giving him key experience, while 31 days between runs keeps him fresh at 133 lb from stall eight; the main risk is his ninth last time out suggesting he needs to bounce back.

runners_data.name: Seagulls Eleven
runners_data.note: Hugo Palmer's four-year-old has a strong winning record on soft but only 9/15 on the sim-going metric, raising a mild concern on this fast ground; a hold-up specialist who ran 10th last time at Goodwood, he needs a very different pace scenario to unlock his finishing effort.
runners_data.comment: Seagulls Eleven boasts two wins and a third in his last five starts, has experience of today's trip and conditions, and 31 days between runs leaves him fresh; the main risk is that unplaced effort last time out.

runners_data.name: Arisaig
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's five-year-old has run six times at Goodwood without winning and his true hold-up style means he is operating out of position in a field loaded with closers; OR=99 is the lowest in the field and the redistribution to midfield does not improve his competitive chance.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Arisaig faces a stiff ask ranked seventh of nine on our figures, and a seventh last time out does little to inspire confidence; she has run over today's trip and going before, and 130 lb from stall four are the neutral facts to weigh.

runners_data.name: Pina Sonata
runners_data.note: James Fanshawe's four-year-old is the least exposed prominent-style runner in the field but her sim-going record of just 2/8 is the most striking concern on this Good to Firm surface; Daniel Muscutt takes the ride and she won at Sandown over 1m on fast ground, so the distance is not an issue.
runners_data.comment: Ranked eighth of nine on our figures and out of the frame on her last two starts, Pina Sonata has plenty to prove, though she has run over today's trip and going before and returns from a 35-day break.

runners_data.name: Zavateri
runners_data.note: Eve Johnson Houghton's three-year-old is the top-rated runner in the field at OR=117, has won four of five on good or faster and is fresh off just a seven-day break; the prominent style and fast-ground profile are ideally matched to the likely race shape, though carrying just 127lbs versus older rivals is the one compensating factor to note.
runners_data.comment: Zavateri posted a second three starts back and has since kept respectable company in his last two outings; experience over today's trip and going works in his favour, and our rating of 120 marks him as the one to beat from stall six carrying 127 lb.

races.paceDynamic: Boiling Point is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine pace rival to press him, Clifford Lee can dictate terms at whatever tempo suits his mount on Good to Firm ground at Goodwood. The prominent trio of Ebt's Guard, Pina Sonata and Zavateri will settle just behind him, creating a compact and controllable early order rather than a contested gallop. This field contains more hold-up types than the race shape can naturally accommodate — Fast Tracker and Arisaig are true hold-up horses redistributed to midfield on the map, but in practice the glut of closers means several will be hunting the same ground late, and the most likely beneficiaries of a clean position are Ebt's Guard and Zavateri who should find the gaps from just off the pace. A sustainable, uncontested lead at a honest but not frantic clip on fast ground heavily favours horses racing prominently or just off the pace with a reliable turn of foot, rather than the deep hold-up horses who will need a strong pace to materialise that never fully develops.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Boiling Point Leads, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Boiling Point dictates a fair but uncontested pace and the race is decided by a finish from the top four at the two-furlong pole.
scenarios.body: Clifford Lee controls fractions from the front, and the modest pace compresses the field so that Ebt's Guard and Zavateri, travelling prominently just behind, have first run entering the final furlong on fast ground that suits a quick, flat kick.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Boiling Point Wins Wire-to-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Boiling Point sets a genuinely measured tempo that dulls the closers' finishing efforts and he quickens off the front on fast ground.
scenarios.body: K. R. Burke's five-year-old has strong course form and his sim-going record of 12/15 reflects a horse who handles this surface well; an uncontested lead on Good to Firm at Goodwood with no pressure is the most favourable scenario for him to sustain his effort to the line.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Breach the Compression
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is fractionally stronger than expected and a gap appears late for hold-up horses to exploit from the two-furlong marker.
scenarios.body: Seagulls Eleven and Naqeeb, genuine hold-up types with strong sim-going records, would need the pace to stretch the field to get their true closer's run; if that unfolds, both arrive with finishing speed that prominent horses may not match.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Midfield Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the field bunches severely and the race turns into a sprint from below the distance, creating a chaotic finish with few holding a clear run.
scenarios.body: A severely compressed field can cause traffic problems for hold-up horses mapped to midfield, and redistributed horses like Fast Tracker and Arisaig — not in their natural roles — are particularly vulnerable; Qirat, who has won at 7f on this course and carries headgear, would be best placed to quicken sharply in the dash.

watchPoints.text: Zavateri carries the highest OR in the field and five career wins have all come on good or faster ground — watch whether Charles Bishop sends him up to sit prominently behind Boiling Point, because that position on fast ground is where the race is likely to be won.

Fast Tracker's 177-day absence is the longest layoff in this field by some margin — Ed Walker has a modest T14 strike rate of 2/38 and a horse returning from nearly six months off, racing out of his natural hold-up role, is a material risk factor.

The hold-up cluster of Naqeeb, Qirat, Seagulls Eleven and Arisaig will all be hunting the same ground late — if Boiling Point controls a steady tempo, watch for traffic congestion and interference entering the final two furlongs as four closers attempt to find gaps simultaneously.

Boiling Point's recent form has been over 9-10 furlongs at Goodwood and softer ground; the drop back to 1m on fast ground is a profile shift — watch whether the pace he sets is genuinely sustainable or whether he slows early and invites a sprint finish he may not win.

Pina Sonata's going record (2/8 on sim-going) stands out as an outlier in a field where most runners are comfortable on fast ground — watch market moves to gauge stable confidence on a surface that has not consistently brought out her best.

races.name: Darley Ebf Maiden Fillies' Stakes (gbb Race)

runners_data.name: Aunt Roberta
runners_data.note: OR-120 filly for George Scott who drops back from a 10f Goodwood run (4th) and a soft-ground effort; her natural instinct is to race from the rear of the field, but with multiple hold-up types in this race she is unlikely to get the clear passage she needs, and 42 days off adds a small fitness question.

runners_data.name: Chimes Of Thunder
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner in the field; David Probert and William Haggas have the option to control tempo entirely, and her Goodwood course experience (three visits) is a significant positive on a track that rewards familiarity.

runners_data.name: Evening Call
runners_data.note: William Haggas's second string who placed on debut over 8f at Goodwood 15 days ago — the step up to 1m2f looks straightforwardly positive given her breeding, and Cieren Fallon is a strong booking; she rates the most likely horse to pressurise or take over from Chimes Of Thunder.

runners_data.name: Marquetry
runners_data.note: Unraced Andrew Balding debutante with Rob Hornby aboard — Balding's 11/66 14-day strike rate signals a yard in good form, and an unknown style could mean she slots anywhere in the race; the absence of form is the sole caveat in a race where experience counts for relatively little in a maiden.

runners_data.name: Mathoura
runners_data.note: Has placed twice over 10f at Goodwood in similar going and clearly handles the track and trip — her true preference is to race from hold-up position, but the overcrowded rear means she will likely race further forward than ideal, which may actually help her in this steadily-run scenario.

runners_data.name: Pseudonym
runners_data.note: Finished a well-beaten ninth on soft ground at 9f for Ollie Sangster and carries a noted tendency to fade in the finish; the switch to Good to Firm is a potential positive, but the same stamina limitation over 1m2f and 79 days off the track make her hard to fancy.

runners_data.name: Queen Of Scotland
runners_data.note: George Boughey debutante with Hector Crouch riding — Boughey's 6/38 14-day form suggests the yard is ticking over, and she could be a well-readied newcomer; no style data means positional uncertainty, which is both the risk and the intrigue.

runners_data.name: Tropical Sands
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's filly has placed over 10f at Goodwood (2nd) and shown consistent form in her three outings — Good to Firm is within her experience range (1/3 on similar ground) and she may be best served by a prominent position just off the leader in this shape.

races.paceDynamic: Chimes Of Thunder is the lone confirmed front-runner in this eight-runner maiden and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, she will dictate from the front at whatever tempo suits William Haggas and David Probert — almost certainly a controlled, measured gallop on Good to Firm ground over 1m2f at Goodwood. That uncontested lead turns this into a steadily-run affair where the pace is sustainable rather than searching, making it very difficult for hold-up horses to generate the momentum they need to close late. The race shape overwhelmingly favours prominent racers and those who can track close to the leader, travelling into the contest rather than chasing it down from off the pace. Aunt Roberta and Mathoura are both genuine hold-up types redistributed to the midfield on the map because the rear is already overcrowded with similar profiles — in reality, neither is likely to secure the prominent berth that would suit them in this shape, and Chimes Of Thunder is the most probable pace-setter with no one to push her.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lone Leader Controls Race
scenarios.trigger: If Chimes Of Thunder is allowed to dictate a moderate, uncontested pace and the hold-up brigade find the winning post arriving before they can close.
scenarios.body: Chimes Of Thunder bowls along in front on her favoured Goodwood track, controlling tempo and preserving energy for the final two furlongs; horses who track closely in second and third positions gain the tactical advantage of cover and a clear run without burning energy chasing a ghost pace.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If a prominent-style runner tracks Chimes Of Thunder through the race and produces a sustained challenge in the straight, pegging back the leader.
scenarios.body: With the pace modest, a horse sitting second or third travelling strongly into the home straight needs only to produce one clean, decisive burst to collar the leader; this rewards horses with enough class to sit close without pulling and enough stamina to see out the 1m2f trip on quick ground.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is fast enough to wind up the early fractions and the leaders tire in the final furlong, opening the door for a hold-up run.
scenarios.body: Aunt Roberta or Mathoura would need the race to genuinely collapse in front of them, which is unlikely given Chimes Of Thunder's ability to manage her own tempo unchallenged; the redistribution of both genuine hold-up types to midfield positions makes this scenario less executable, as neither will be ideally placed to produce a true late sprint.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Debutante Springs Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If one of the unraced runners — Marquetry or Queen Of Scotland — shows natural class and tactical versatility to overcome inexperience.
scenarios.body: A well-bred, well-prepared debutante from Andrew Balding or George Boughey could slot into a prominent position and benefit from the steady pace, needing only to handle the race experience itself; with an unknown style rating and no form to oppose, the upside is real but the probability is low against more exposed rivals.

watchPoints.text: Chimes Of Thunder sets the entire tactical agenda unchallenged — if she is allowed to bowl along at a low-pressure gallop, horses with hold-up styles like Aunt Roberta and Mathoura simply will not generate enough late momentum to catch her.

Aunt Roberta and Mathoura are both mapped to midfield but are genuine hold-up types by style — watch how both jockeys react at the start, as either forcing them forward or dropping them to the rear produces a style mismatch that harms their chance.

Evening Call is William Haggas's more interesting runner over a trip that should suit her better than her debut 8f — if she travels strongly into the home straight, she represents the primary danger to the leader and is worth monitoring early in the straight.

Both debutantes Marquetry and Queen Of Scotland have no public form to assess — watch the market moves in the 30 minutes before the race, as money for either could reveal stable confidence that the form data cannot show.

The going is confirmed Good to Firm throughout the card — any horse whose Timeform or RPR history skews toward soft or good ground carries a subtle class-adjustment risk, with Pseudonym's sole run on soft being the clearest example.

races.name: Virgin Bet Daily Price Boosts Handicap Stakes (gbbplus Race)

runners_data.name: Caprelo
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with solid course form at this exact 1m6f Goodwood trip, having won here at Staplefield too; Rob Hornby booked, trainer Morrison quiet at 0/7 in 14 days but the horse returns 52 days fresh and this trip/course combination suits perfectly.
runners_data.comment: Caprelo shaped with promise when second three starts back and has experience of today's trip and going to call on, with our rating edging him clear of his mark; the concern is five weeks off the track and consecutive minor efforts since that placed run.

runners_data.name: Scarlet Moon
runners_data.note: The confirmed pace-setter; Archie Watson in fair recent form (2/20 T14) and Goodwood course form is encouraging, though sim-going record of 2W5P from 15 runs suggests she usually finds one or two too good from the front.
runners_data.comment: Scarlet Moon has won in recent starts but a subsequent unplaced effort clouds his claims, and he sits ninth of twelve on our figures, making him difficult to fancy at the weights with 135 lb to carry; he does at least bring distance and going experience to the table.

runners_data.name: Bright Legend
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse stepping down from 20f trips, which could be a stamina edge over this 1m6f; ran at Goodwood recently (7th over 20f) and Clifford Lee takes over, with the return 10 days quick but not alarming given the horse ran well fresh before.
runners_data.comment: Bright Legend is the top-rated runner here and showed what he is capable of with a win five starts back, while a fourth last time out — just 10 days ago — suggests he remains in form carrying 135 lb.

runners_data.name: Appier
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist who found only two too good over 14f at Goodwood on last completed course run and has a winning record on soft; Tony Carroll's 3/36 T14 rate is modest, but David Probert is a strong booking and the horse handles quick ground adequately.
runners_data.comment: Placed third last time out and a winner two starts back, Appier has experience of today's distance and going in his favour, though a sixth and an unplaced run before that win temper confidence; fit enough on 36 days off, he carries 134 lb here.

runners_data.name: Russian Rumour
runners_data.note: Strong each-way profile at Goodwood — three course runs, all placed — and the sim-going figures (2W6P from 9 runs) are the best in the field for Good to Firm; Olivia Tubb's 5lb claim is a significant weight advantage for a hold-up type that clearly relishes this track.
runners_data.comment: Russian Rumour has been a model of consistency, finishing third three of her last four starts and winning one start back from that, and she has experience over today's trip and going; the concern is whether she can convert that solid placed form into a victory under 133 lb.

runners_data.name: Zachary Hickes
runners_data.note: Lightly raced 4-year-old stepping up markedly in trip from 10-12f to 1m6f, which is unproven territory; Roger Varian sends him from a yard in excellent 14-day form (6/17) and Jack Mitchell is a confident booking, but the stamina question is real.
runners_data.comment: Landed a win last time out to arrive here in form, and having run over today's going before he is no stranger to the conditions; however, ranked eighth of twelve on speed figures, he faces a stiff ask off 133 lb against stronger company.

runners_data.name: Gooloogong
runners_data.note: Prominent-running stayer who won over this exact 1m6f trip at Staplefield and placed at Goodwood over 20f; trainer Baker quiet (0/5 T14) but Benoit de la Sayette is a sharp tactical rider who will be able to sit Gooloogong in a position that suits the race shape.
runners_data.comment: Ranked tenth of twelve on our figures and carrying 133 lb, Gooloogong is hard to fancy despite a third last time out and a win four starts back; he has experience of today's distance and going, but his speed rating of 68 leaves plenty to find.

runners_data.name: Arcturus Flame
runners_data.note: In excellent recent form (2nd, 3rd, 2nd in last three) and wears a tongue-tie; a genuine hold-up horse by nature, the crowded rear-of-field means he is mapped to midfield — racing closer than ideal, which may blunt his trademark finish if he cannot drop back into his comfort zone.
runners_data.comment: Arcturus Flame arrives on the back of a runner-up finish last time out, with distance and going experience working in his favour and a rating of 84 suggesting he is well treated on official figures — the main concern is that he remains winless in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Mr Freedom
runners_data.note: Prominent handler with Goodwood course experience, though recent efforts at 12-14f suggest the step to 1m6f is asking a question; Sheena West's 1/4 T14 rate is modest and the 59-day absence after a modest run means fitness needs proving before this becomes a serious threat.
runners_data.comment: Mr Freedom arrives on a 59-day break and is yet to win in recent starts, with a distant eighth last time out offsetting a third three starts back; experience over today's trip and going helps, though 132 lb is a stiff ask for a gelding rated 77.

runners_data.name: Taritino
runners_data.note: In-form stayer with four wins and a second from last five Goodwood runs — an outstanding course record; however, his true style is hold-up and the congestion behind means he may not get the position he needs, which is the key risk against his otherwise excellent profile for this track and trip.
runners_data.comment: Taritino won two of his last five starts, with consecutive victories three and four starts back, though he has returned a pair of fourths in his two most recent outings; he has run over today's trip and going, and 25 days off should leave him fresh enough to reverse that slide.

runners_data.name: Educator
runners_data.note: A horse in the best recent form of his life (two wins in last three), fitted with a hood, and Daniel Tudhope is a top booking; by inclination a closer, but the surplus of hold-up types means he may race closer to the pace than he'd like — that said, his recent wins from similar positions suggest he is versatile enough to cope.
runners_data.comment: Ranked 11 of 12 on our figures, Educator faces a stiff ask under 130 lb, yet his recent form reads better than his ranking suggests — a winner two starts back and again last time out, with experience over today's trip and going at least lending familiarity.

runners_data.name: Two Plus Two
runners_data.note: The co-pace-setter carrying 116lbs (OR 60) — dramatically lower-rated than the rest of the field; Gina Mangan takes the ride for Ed de Giles, and while Two Plus Two has won at Goodwood over 14f, the likelihood is that Scarlet Moon's greater quality will see her dropped or weakened before the turn.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Two Plus Two is hard to fancy despite a record that shows a second last time out and a winner five starts back; he has experience over today's trip and going, but that profile offers only slim encouragement.

races.paceDynamic: Scarlet Moon and Two Plus Two are the confirmed pace-setters over this 1m6f Good to Firm Goodwood trip, and with two genuine leaders in a 12-runner field a contested early gallop is the most likely outcome — neither is likely to yield without a fight, ensuring the race is run at an honest, sustained tempo from the outset. Scarlet Moon has course form at Goodwood and comes back from a longer trip, while Two Plus Two is significantly lower-rated (OR 60) and may prove the weaker of the two when pressed for real early speed. The resulting honest gallop over a stiff 1m6f on quick ground is a shape that typically rewards horses who sit close to the pace in a prominent or mid-prominent role — giving them cover from the early battle without expending energy fighting for position, then having enough left to quicken when the front pair tire. The field holds more hold-up horses than the map can accommodate at the rear — Arcturus Flame, Taritino, and Educator are genuine closers pushed into midfield representation, meaning the true beneficiaries of a prominent sit are Caprelo and Gooloogong, with the pace-forward profile most favoured in this shape.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Honest Pace Suits Prominent
scenarios.trigger: If Scarlet Moon and Two Plus Two trade honest fractions and set a true gallop, softening the race for those who track just off the pace.
scenarios.body: The two leaders burn each other up over the first mile, leaving those who settled just behind in a position to pounce off the bend; Caprelo's consistent Goodwood form at this trip and Gooloogong's proven stamina make them natural beneficiaries of this shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: One Leader Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Scarlet Moon sees off Two Plus Two early and controls a strong but measured gallop, conserving enough to resist.
scenarios.body: With the lower-rated Two Plus Two dropped out or outpaced, Scarlet Moon controls the fractions and the race becomes a test of stamina at a more manageable clip; Scarlet Moon's Goodwood course form and strong sim-going record give her the best chance of holding on under Pierre-Louis Jamin.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the leaders set a genuinely fierce gallop that blows the race wide open for hold-up types tracking from midfield.
scenarios.body: Russian Rumour, who has strong course form at Goodwood and a fine record on Good to Firm, is best placed to finish powerfully if the pace is truly testing; Educator and Taritino, though genuinely hold-up types mapped into midfield, could also benefit if they secure better position than expected.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Muddled Pace Lottery
scenarios.trigger: If the two leaders fail to produce a truly honest gallop and the tempo fluctuates, creating a bunched finish.
scenarios.body: An uneven gallop compresses the field and brings quirky or inconsistent types into play, reducing the advantage of any single style and introducing wider market outsiders; Bright Legend's versatile staying profile and Appier's tactical flexibility could make them awkward threats in a scrappy finish.

watchPoints.text: Scarlet Moon and Two Plus Two are both confirmed front-runners — watch how quickly they establish the pace in the first two furlongs, as a fierce duel will collapse their chances and dramatically boost Caprelo and Gooloogong tracking just behind.

Russian Rumour with Olivia Tubb's 5lb claim may be the best-weighted horse in the race given her Goodwood course form — watch for her to be produced wide and late if the gallop is genuinely searching.

Taritino's Goodwood course record is exceptional (4W from recent runs) but if he cannot drop to the rear in a field this size, he will race in a compressed midfield that blunts his finish — watch where Taylor Fisher positions him in the first half-mile.

Zachary Hickes is stepping from 10f to 1m6f — a dramatic trip extension — but Roger Varian's 6/17 14-day strike rate is the best in this field; watch for early market moves that suggest connections are confident the stamina is there.

Educator's hood is worn for the first time at this level — watch for any signs of early-race agitation or uncharacteristic keenness, as a keen hold-up horse in a field this size could find himself racing in a position that wastes his proven finishing kick.

races.name: Virgin Bet Supports Safe Gambling Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: All Ways Glamorous
runners_data.note: Five-year-old mare with four wins at Goodwood's 5f on similar ground, sitting on a perfect course-track combination; races prominently, has Gina Mangan booked, and the 21-day break on a horse who returns fresh to this course is a strong positive angle.
runners_data.comment: Back-to-back wins two and three starts back make All Ways Glamorous interesting, but a fourth last time out and our rating placing him last-but-one in a field of eight make him hard to fancy, even if he has experience over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Lexington Blitz
runners_data.note: Front-runner equipped with blinkers who won this course-distance-going combination last time and will seek to bolt for the lead under Jack Mitchell; the risk is Democracy Dilemma forcing him into a war he cannot sustain, which is the central pace question for the race.

runners_data.name: Toca Madera
runners_data.note: Daniel Tudhope partners a horse who has dominated 5f Goodwood entries in terms of runs but converted only once, and his hold-up style means he needs the contested lead to fully materialise; the step back to 5f from two recent 6f efforts is worth monitoring for fitness sharpness.
runners_data.comment: Toca Madera showed plenty of promise when third two starts back, and with experience of today's trip and going under his belt, he arrives here fresh on a seven-day turnaround with our rating putting him right in contention; the risk is that he has been winless in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Democracy Dilemma
runners_data.note: Visored front-runner for Robert Cowell who has a patchy recent record including a 20th-place effort, and while he won over C&D his form suggests he is vulnerable when the pressure comes on early — his direct clash with stablemate Lexington Blitz is the crux of the pace map.
runners_data.comment: Fifth last time out and fourth two starts back, Democracy Dilemma arrives 21 days fresh with distance and going experience to call on, though winless in his last six starts, carrying 138 lb from stall five may test his resolution at a rating of 95.

runners_data.name: Naana's Sparkle
runners_data.note: Tongue-tied four-year-old who won at Goodwood 5f on her penultimate start and ran to figures that make her competitive off OR 94; Kieran O'Neill rides a horse who travels prominently and is course-proven, making her one of the most natural beneficiaries if the pace duel plays out as expected.

runners_data.name: Kylian
runners_data.note: Visored hold-up type for Robert Cowell who has placed at Goodwood 5f before but whose recent form string shows little consistency and his best sim-going record is the thinnest in the field at 8/15 qualifiers; needs the race to truly fall apart to get involved.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Kylian at least returns on a quick turnaround of 13 days and has run over today's trip and going before, but a fourth last time out represents his best recent effort and the weight of 132 lb from stall 3 makes life no easier.

runners_data.name: Dyonisos
runners_data.note: Ran a strong winning race at Goodwood 5f on Good to Firm earlier this year and David Probert has course knowledge here; races in a prominent-to-midfield style that sits naturally just behind the lead group, and the 32-day break is the only mild concern on a horse who clearly goes well fresh.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Dyonisos is hard to fancy off 131 lb from stall 7, and his latest run was a ninth; however, he does own a win in his last six starts and has run over today's distance and going before, offering slim consolation.

runners_data.name: Dream Composer
runners_data.note: An eight-year-old who has shown genuine ability at Goodwood 5f and whose trainer Tony Carroll is in a productive 14-day window; he is a confirmed hold-up type by nature but with so many pace-oriented horses in this field, he is unlikely to find his natural rearward position and that style dislocation tempers his prospects even if his raw form is competitive.
runners_data.comment: Dream Composer won three starts back and has run over today's trip and going, but a fourth last time out and a fifth two starts back suggest he is finding the opposition stiff at present; 127 lb from stall six is no aid, though the step up in our rating to 95 hints at residual ability.

races.paceDynamic: Lexington Blitz and Democracy Dilemma are the two confirmed front-runners in this 5f Goodwood sprint, and with both trained by Robert Cowell they are unlikely to defer to one another — a genuine early duel is the most probable outcome, setting a brisk, unrelenting tempo from the gates. That contested lead dynamic compresses the advantage for the pace-setters and historically at Goodwood over 5f on Good to Firm, a strong early gallop funnels the race into the hands of prominent-to-midfield closers who can travel efficiently and pick up off a true pace. All Ways Glamorous and Naana's Sparkle, as legitimate prominent types, are best placed to exploit that shape — they can sit just behind the scrapping leaders and deliver their challenge without burning fuel in the early battle. The field also holds more pace than this map can naturally accommodate, with Dream Composer — a true hold-up type — pushed into a midfield slot on the visualisation; in reality, the race shape will see prominent types crowding the early positions, meaning genuine closers may find wider berths but cleaner air late.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Lead, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Lexington Blitz and Democracy Dilemma fight for the front and burn each other out, handing the race to a prominent tracker.
scenarios.body: The two Robert Cowell front-runners engage in a speed duel that drains both, leaving All Ways Glamorous and Naana's Sparkle able to stride past in the final furlong on Good to Firm ground that rewards relentless galloping. Both prominent types have strong Goodwood 5f form and will race at an economical pace just off the lead, putting themselves in the ideal position to pick up the pieces.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Clears Field
scenarios.trigger: If one of the Cowell pace-setters — most likely Lexington Blitz — gains a clean break and dictates a controlled lead without being pressured into a true duel.
scenarios.body: A solo leader on Good to Firm at Goodwood over 5f can carve out a rhythm that is surprisingly hard to peg back, especially if rivals are slow to organise their challenges; Lexington Blitz's blinkers and recent course win underline his aptitude for this scenario. Democracy Dilemma's inconsistent record in similar fields means Lexington Blitz is the likelier beneficiary if one front-runner gains supremacy.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace explodes to such a degree that the race falls apart and true hold-up horses are gifted a collapsing lead to run through.
scenarios.body: Toca Madera and Kylian sit deepest in the field and would require a genuinely suicidal early pace to generate enough late momentum to overhaul rivals who have been travelling more comfortably throughout. This scenario carries a discount because Dream Composer — the other hold-up type — has been redistributed and is unlikely to secure genuine rearward cover, reducing the density of proven closers who can truly benefit.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Grinder Grinds Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is moderate despite the two front-runners and the race becomes a searching test of finishing power rather than a collapse of the leaders.
scenarios.body: Dyonisos, with a winning Goodwood 5f run in his recent history and consistent Good to Firm form, has the raw profile to grind through a slowly evolving contest, though his inconsistency makes this a low-probability route. Dream Composer's redistribution to midfield means even if this shape partially materialises, he will not be racing from his natural position and his chance is tempered accordingly.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Lexington Blitz or Democracy Dilemma blinks first out of the stalls — if both jump cleanly and neither concedes, the duel will be intense and the prominent horses directly behind them become the primary dangers.

Naana's Sparkle carries a tongue-tie and is running just 10 days after her last race; monitor market moves in the final hour as any market confidence here would signal stable satisfaction following that quick return.

Toca Madera has been running over 6f in his two most recent starts and drops back to 5f today — watch his early gallop to see whether he travels with his usual rhythm or gets outpaced before he can engage his finish.

Robert Cowell saddles three runners (Lexington Blitz, Democracy Dilemma, Kylian) from a 1/11 14-day strike rate — his stable's tactical intentions are worth watching in the paddock, particularly regarding which runner receives preferential positioning instructions.

The going report confirms Good to Firm for the 4:55 5f race, firmer than the declared Good — any horse with a going concern flag flagged earlier in the week for fast ground should be rechecked against final declarations for any late withdrawals that could ease the pace dynamics.
